# FIPS Codes

## FIPS Codes

The US Data files use [FIPS Codes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIPS_county_code)
to identify counties

- Standardized codes to represent geographic regions
  - From Census block groups (~1000 people) to states
- State FIPS codes are two numeric characters
- County FIPS codes are three numeric characters
- The combination of State and County FIPS
  - 5 numeric characters
  - Uniquely identifies each county in the US
  
## Why FIPS Codes?

- FIPS provide a standardized, unique identifier for geographic units in the US
- We are in county `24033`
- Contrast with
  - Prince Georges
  - Prince George's
  - PG County


# The `usmap` Package

## The `usmap` Package

`usmap` has facilities for dealing with US geospatial data

- Create Maps of state/county data
- Look up proper names of states and counties using FIPS codes (easy)
- Convert State/County names into FIPS codes (hard)

## Using `usmap`

To use `usmap`

- Install the `usmap` packge
```r
install.packages("usmap")
```
- Load the library
```r
library(usmap)
```

# Looking Up Information for a FIPS

## Getting names from FIPS codes

`usmap` provides a function for looking up geographic entitiy names

```r
fips_info(
  fips=<fips>,
  [data_year=<year>])
```

- `<fips>` A FIPS code to look up
- `<year>` Year from which to pull FIPS data (if they change)


## Example - Look Up Information for a FIPS

Looking up a single name
```{r}
#| echo: true
fips_info("24033")
```
Extract the individual components with double-brackets
```{r}
#| echo: true
fips_info("24033")[["abbr"]]
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
fips_info("24033")[["county"]]
```


## Using with `mutate()`

You can _technically_ use `fips_info()` with `mutate()`

- Lookups are slow can can take a long time
  - Best practice is to use `distinct()` on your FIPS codes first
  - Use a `join_*()` to combine info back in
- `fips_info()` returns an empty list if the FIPS is `NA` or invalid
  - R skips these when pulling results together in `mutate()`
  - You'll have fewer rows than your full dataset
  - `mutate()` will fail with an error message

## Using with `mutate()`

If you want to use `fips_info()` with mutate, create a wrapper that checks for invalid FIPS

- I've provided this code as a template to get this done
- It probably doesn't make sense


## Example wrapper function for `mutate()`

```{r}
#| echo: true
get_fips_county <- function(fips, ...) {
  # If NA or not 5 characters, reutrn NA
  if(is.na(fips) | !str_detect(fips,"^[0-9]{5}$")) result = NA_character_
  else {
    # Look up the FIPS
    county_info = fips_info(fips, ...)
    # If we get an empty response, return NA
    if(nrow(county_info) == 0) result = NA_character_
    # Otherwise extract the county and reuturn it
    else result = county_info[["county"]]
  }
  return(result)
}
```

## Example wrapper function for `mutate()`

Same thing for state abbriviations 

```{r}
#| echo: true
get_fips_state <- function(fips, ...) {
  # If NA or not 5 characters, reutrn NA
  if(is.na(fips) | !str_detect(fips,"^[0-9]{5}$")) result = NA_character_
  else {
    # Look up the FIPS
    state_info = fips_info(fips, ...)
    # If we get an empty response, return NA
    if(nrow(state_info) == 0) result = NA_character_
    # Otherwise extract the county and reuturn it
    else result = state_info[["abbr"]]
  }
  return(result)
}
```

## Example - Using with `mutate()`

You need to use the `map_*()` function to get R to perform this operation one row at a time

- Again, we haven't covered this, but the code is a template for accomplishing the task
```r
noaa_tmp |>
  distinct(StateCountyFIPS) |>
  mutate(
    county_name = map_chr(StateCountyFIPS,get_fips_county),
    state_abbr = map_chr(StateCountyFIPS,get_fips_state)
  ) -> fips_map

noaa_tmp |>
  left_join(fips_map,join_by(StateCounty_FIPS)) |>
  select(Year,Month,Value,StateCountyFIPS,county_name)
```

## Example - Using with `mutate()`
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
# Example eval on a small subset to speed computation time
noaa_tmp |>
  distinct(StateCountyFIPS) |>
  slice(1:20) |>
  mutate(
    county_name = map_chr(StateCountyFIPS,get_fips_county),
    state_abbr = map_chr(StateCountyFIPS,get_fips_state)
  ) -> fips_map

noaa_tmp |>
  inner_join(fips_map,join_by(StateCountyFIPS)) |>
  select(Year,Month,Value,StateCountyFIPS,county_name,state_abbr) |>
  glimpse()
```

:::{.callout-tip}

### The number of observations is reduced in this example

The code above limits the counties it translates to the first 20. Looking up
county info is slow and I've limited the number of counties processed in this
example using `slice()` to speed up computation. 
:::

## Create a map of temperatures

Create maps using `plot_usmap()`

- An extension of `ggplot()`
- Creates a plot and adds the map layer
- Requires several arguments


# Creating maps

## Creating Maps

The US Map package can be used to create maps

- Creates maps of data from US states
- Automatically insets Alaska and Hawaii
- Uses either state or county data
- Indexed by FIPS

## Creating maps

Example usage

```r
plot_usmap(
  data=<data>, 
  regions="<county|state>", 
  )
```

- `<data>` A dataframe with columns
  - `fips` The State (2-character) or County (5-character) FIPS as text
  - `values` A column of values to plot
- `"<county|state>"` Specifies geography to use for plotting

## Creating maps

`plot_usmap()` is an extension of `ggplot()`

- Identical to `ggplot()` plus a map layer
- You can use other `ggplot()` functions and aesthetics to customize the 
visualization
- There are some other useful options as well

Let's create a map of temperatures in July 2025


## Create data for a map of temperatures

First, create a dataset of temperatures in only July 2025

```{r filter-month}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
noaa_tmp |>
  filter(Year == 2025 & Month == "Jul") |>
  rename(
    fips = StateCountyFIPS,
    values = Value  
  ) -> noaa_tmp_jul2025
```

## First map of temperatures

```{r map-1}
#| fig-align: "center"
#| fig-height: 7
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true

plot_usmap(
  data=noaa_tmp_jul2025, 
  regions="county"
  )
```

## Fixing Problems

**Problems**

- No data for AK/HI
  - `exclude=` argument
- County outlines make it hard to read
  - `color=` layer property
- Color scale is tough to read
  - `scale_fill_*()`
- What's up with CT?
  - ???


## A Better Map

```{r map-penultimate}
#| fig-align: "center"
#| fig-height: 7
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
plot_usmap(
  data=noaa_tmp_jul2025, 
  regions="county", 
  color=NA,
  exclude=c("HI","AK")
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option="turbo") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    fill="Average\nTemperature"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## What's up with CT?

Connecticut is gray in the map -- No data. Why?

- The US Census bureau redivided CT in 2024
- Split former 8 counties into 9 planning regions
- New planning regions have different FIPS codes
- By default `usmap` uses the most recent map
- Old FIPS codes don't match new values in the map

Force an older map with `data_year=`

## An Even Better Map

```{r map-final}
#| fig-align: "center"
#| fig-height: 7
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
plot_usmap(
  data=noaa_tmp_jul2025, 
  regions="county", 
  color=NA,
  exclude=c("HI","AK"),
  data_year=2021
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option="turbo") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    fill="Average\nTemperature"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
